requirements.objective: Define ArchitectureDesign 0.1.0 as one deterministic DevRelay module that converts an approved RequirementsBaseline into either a new architecture baseline candidate or a proposed change to an existing architecture, using a configured chain of bounded, replaceable adapters.

in: One ArchitectureDesign module with establish-baseline and design-change operations.
Deterministic operation routing from persisted project architecture state.
A prerequisite ArchitectureDiscovery route for existing repositories without a current architecture snapshot.
Ordered designer, modeler, and decision-recorder adapter steps.
Step handoffs, clarification checkpoints, native-source preservation, validation, conformance fixtures, and documentation.
V1 adapter manifests for Spec Kit plan, OpenSpec design, Structurizr, and MADR.
out: Requirements approval logic beyond the recorded Requirements Gate.
Architecture approval or ArchitectureBaseline promotion, which belongs to the Architecture Gate.
Detailed OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, protobuf, database, or other interface contract generation.
Architecture enforcement, security review, performance verification, task decomposition, code generation, or integration.
Installation or execution of upstream Spec Kit, OpenSpec, Structurizr, or MADR tooling.
A distributed scheduler, agent framework, provider wrapper, package marketplace, or model-specific workflow.

assumptions.statement: ArchitectureDesign 0.1.0 has not been published, so the invalid provisional single-operation definition can be replaced without preserving it as a released contract.
Supporting architecture sections and native files are subordinate content or attachments inside one primary module output.
The separate Architecture Gate owns human approval and promotion or update of ArchitectureBaseline.
This run uses the configured OpenSpec agent-command bridge for requirements work and does not claim OpenSpec CLI execution.

constraints: DevRelay Core, not a model or adapter, selects the operation, configured adapters, sequence, validation path, and gate progression.
ArchitectureDesign must consume an approved RequirementsBaseline.
Module contracts remain provider-neutral and cannot branch on adapter or upstream-tool identifiers in generic core.
Every runtime boundary uses immutable artifact references and exact adapter versions.
ArchitectureDesign produces candidates only; it cannot approve or promote its own result.
The implementation must preserve compatibility with RequirementsGathering 0.1.0.
The first pass must remain small enough to prove modular composition without creating a general workflow platform.

requirements.statement: DevRelay must expose exactly one ArchitectureDesign module whose purpose is to convert approved requirements into either a new architecture baseline candidate or a proposed change to an existing architecture.
requirements.rationale: A single semantic boundary avoids artificial greenfield/brownfield module duplication.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The registered module identifier is architecture-design at version 0.1.0.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Register the module through the generic registry and inspect its immutable identity.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The module never emits an approved ArchitectureBaseline.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect declared output ports and reject undeclared baseline output.

requirements.statement: ArchitectureDesign must expose exactly the establish-baseline and design-change operations under one shared module contract.
requirements.rationale: The operations have distinct preconditions and primary results while sharing orchestration and artifact semantics.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: No provisional design operation remains in the ArchitectureDesign definition.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Assert the sorted operation identifiers equal establish-baseline and design-change.

requirements.statement: DevRelay Core must deterministically select establish-baseline when no ArchitectureBaseline exists and design-change when an ArchitectureBaseline exists, using persisted project architecture state rather than model judgment.
requirements.rationale: Routing is workflow authority and must be replayable, testable, and independent of implementation engines.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Greenfield-unbaselined and existing-discovered-unbaselined states select establish-baseline.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run router fixtures for both state values.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Baselined state selects design-change and an invocation cannot override that decision.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the route/invocation binding negative test.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Unknown, duplicate, or ambiguous routing rules fail closed.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run deterministic router negative tests.

requirements.statement: An existing repository with no ArchitectureBaseline and no CurrentArchitectureSnapshot must route to the ArchitectureDiscovery prerequisite; its snapshot then permits establish-baseline.
requirements.rationale: Repository structure is evidence but is not an approved architecture baseline.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Existing-undiscovered state produces a prerequisite route and cannot start ArchitectureDesign.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the prerequisite and invocation-blocking router tests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The prerequisite declares CurrentArchitectureSnapshot as its required output contract.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect the ArchitectureDesign routing declaration.

requirements.statement: Each ArchitectureDesign operation must execute an ordered designer, modeler, decision-recorder adapter chain with validated handoffs and exactly one terminal module result.
requirements.rationale: Best-in-class capabilities can be swapped independently only when step boundaries and sequencing are explicit.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The registry resolves all configured steps before execution and invokes them only in declared order.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run chain resolution and in-memory execution tests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Missing, duplicate, reordered, incompatible, or nonterminal step results are rejected.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run negative chain conformance tests.

sourceRefs.location: Clarification 3: adapter sequence and Core authority

requirements.statement: The V1 default chain must use SpecKitPlanAdapter for establish-baseline or OpenSpecDesignAdapter for design-change, followed by StructurizrAdapter and MADRAdapter.
requirements.rationale: These are selected V1 implementations of stable semantic step contracts, not hard-coded kernel behavior.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The baseline example pins Spec Kit plan, Structurizr, and MADR adapter manifests with exact versions and step roles.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Resolve the establish-baseline invocation fixture.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The change example pins OpenSpec design, Structurizr, and MADR adapter manifests with exact versions and step roles.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Resolve the design-change invocation fixture.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Replacing a compatible step adapter requires configuration only and no generic-core identifier branch.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the adapter-swap fixture and core special-case scan.

requirements.statement: A successful establish-baseline invocation must return exactly one ArchitectureDraft, and a successful design-change invocation must return exactly one ArchitectureChangeSetDraft.
requirements.rationale: One primary candidate makes the module boundary and downstream Architecture Gate unambiguous.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Successful result contracts allow and require only the operation-specific primary output.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate both success results and reject extra top-level outputs.

requirements.statement: ArchitectureDraft and ArchitectureChangeSetDraft must contain or immutably reference technical design, architecture model, diagrams, interface intent, architecture constraints, decision records, and native artifacts.
requirements.rationale: Supporting work remains complete and traceable without becoming separate module outcomes.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Both canonical primary artifact fixtures expose all seven named sections.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate fixtures against the architecture artifact schema.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A section may be embedded or attached by immutable artifact reference, but cannot be absent or both forms at once.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run section-union negative schema tests.

requirements.statement: ProjectArchitectureState must distinguish greenfield-unbaselined, existing-undiscovered, existing-discovered-unbaselined, and baselined states and bind any required snapshot or baseline by exact artifact reference.
requirements.rationale: Closed explicit state prevents inference from repository contents or conversational memory.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each valid state variant accepts only its required references.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate positive and contradictory state fixtures.

requirements.statement: Every step handoff and primary output must preserve exact input, adapter, native-source, normalization, and output provenance without relying on conversational or provider session memory.
requirements.rationale: Traceable handoffs are required for resume, audit, swapping, and trustworthy normalization.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A successful chain exposes step results bound to the exact invocation, inputs, adapter version, and produced artifact digests.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run handoff validation and digest-mismatch tests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Native artifacts are subordinate to the primary candidate and retain warnings for unmapped or unexecuted native behavior.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect and validate both primary artifact fixtures.

sourceRefs.location: Workflow instruction and Clarification 3: Core authority

requirements.statement: ArchitectureDesign must capture interface intent and architectural constraints, while detailed API, event, data, and protocol contracts remain in downstream ContractGeneration.
requirements.rationale: Architecture should define boundaries without collapsing a later deterministic lifecycle stage.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Canonical artifacts require interface intent but do not require OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, protobuf, or database-schema payloads.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect the schema and documentation boundary.

requirements.statement: Blocking ambiguity at any ArchitectureDesign step must emit portable clarification requests and a complete continuation; resume must bind the matching responses and exact prior state.
requirements.rationale: A multi-step effectful module must resume without hidden native-tool or chat state.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Clarification output contains the request set and continuation but no primary architecture candidate.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Validate a clarification result fixture.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Continuation and response inputs are required together and bind the exact paused stage.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run input-rule and artifact semantic validation tests.

sourceRefs.location: Workflow instruction: normal user-facing module workflow

requirements.statement: Module validation must establish structural and semantic completeness, while a separate Architecture Gate decides clarity, fitness, approval, and promotion or update of ArchitectureBaseline.
requirements.rationale: Generation and progression authority must remain separate deterministic stages.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: ArchitectureDesign outputs are explicitly candidates and cannot claim gate approval.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect module outcomes and documentation.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Progression documentation requires a passing Architecture Gate bound to the exact candidate digest.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Review the end-to-end workflow example.

sourceRefs.location: Clarifications 2 and 3: approval and Core progression

requirements.statement: Each adapter manifest must bind only the relevant upstream capability for its declared ArchitectureDesign step; DevRelay must not treat an upstream repository's full workflow as one module.
requirements.rationale: Bounded capabilities preserve module ownership and permit independent best-in-class replacement.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Spec Kit exposes only planning for the designer step and OpenSpec exposes only design for the designer step in ArchitectureDesign.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect the adapter manifests and bounded native schemas.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Structurizr and MADR manifests implement only their modeler and decision-recorder steps.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Inspect and register the adapter manifests.

requirements.statement: The implementation must include positive and negative schema, routing, registry, chain, artifact, clarification, provenance, backward-compatibility, and core-neutrality tests.
requirements.rationale: Determinism and replaceability require executable evidence, not naming conventions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The full DevRelay test suite passes.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run npm.cmd test.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: RequirementsGathering 0.1.0 fixtures continue to resolve and validate unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the pre-existing RequirementsGathering conformance tests.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Generic core contains no ArchitectureDesign or adapter identifier branches.
acceptanceCriteria.verification: Run the source neutrality scan.

sourceRefs.location: Canonical definition and approved build authorization

dependencies: RequirementsGathering 0.1.0 and its approved RequirementsBaseline contract.
The generic ModuleDefinition, ModulePlugin, ModuleInvocation, ModuleResult, ArtifactRef, Evidence, schema compiler, and content-digest contracts.
A downstream Architecture Gate before candidate promotion.
A future ArchitectureDiscovery module or compatible prerequisite implementation for existing-undiscovered state.
risks: A chain abstraction that is too general could expand DevRelay into a workflow platform instead of a small module runner.
Weak step contracts could allow native tool output or conversational state to leak across adapters.
Treating a repository snapshot as an architecture baseline would make changes unauditable.
Embedding full OpenSpec or Spec Kit workflows would duplicate stages and prevent independent module replacement.
A canonical architecture artifact that is too prescriptive could merely replace one upstream methodology with another.
Contract fixtures prove boundary compatibility but do not prove live upstream CLI interoperability.
deliverables: Approved ArchitectureDesign RequirementsBaseline and user-visible clarification record.
Generic deterministic operation router and ordered adapter-chain support.
ArchitectureDesign module definition with establish-baseline and design-change.
Canonical project-state, routing, discovery, draft, change-set, step-work, and clarification artifact contracts.
Spec Kit plan, OpenSpec design, Structurizr, and MADR bounded adapter manifests.
Representative invocations, step results, primary outputs, and end-to-end workflow documentation.
Conformance, negative, regression, and core-neutrality tests.
